stem: A 48-year-old woman has painful mouth erosions followed by fragile blisters on her trunk that break easily, leaving raw areas. Rubbing normal-looking skin makes the top layer slide off. A skin biopsy shows cells separating just above the basal layer, which stays attached like a row of tombstones.
oneliner: 48F + painful oral erosions → fragile flaccid blisters + skin slides with rubbing + split just above basal layer, tombstone row → what's attacked?
ask: Antibodies against which structure most likely cause this?

options.A: Desmosomes joining basal to suprabasal keratinocytes
options.B: Hemidesmosomes joining basal cells to the basement membrane
options.C: Tight junctions in the stratum granulosum

whyNot.B: **Bullous pemphigoid**: tense blisters, mouth usually spared, split **below** the epidermis
whyNot.C: Not an autoimmune blistering target; **no tombstoning**
whyNot.D: **Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita**: blisters at trauma sites, scarring
whyNot.E: Gap junction defects cause **hearing loss and skin thickening** syndromes, not blisters

why: **Mouth involvement + flaccid blisters + positive Nikolsky + split above the basal layer** = pemphigus vulgaris. IgG against **desmoglein** breaks the **desmosomes** that hold keratinocytes together (acantholysis).
chain: Split just above the basal layer
Flaccid blisters, Nikolsky sign, mouth erosions

idea.rule: Desmosomes hold cells to cells (pemphigus); hemidesmosomes hold cells to the basement membrane (pemphigoid).
also: Staph scalded skin: toxin cuts desmoglein 1 (no mouth)
Bullous pemphigoid: BP180/BP230, tense blisters

stem: A 14-year-old girl has had blackheads and red bumps on her forehead and cheeks that have worsened over 8 months, starting soon after her first menstrual period. She uses no new cosmetics, and a food diary shows no pattern of flare-ups. There is no itching and no lesions on the trunk.
oneliner: 14F + facial blackheads and inflamed papules since menarche + no new cosmetics, no dietary link → why?
ask: Which of the following best explains her skin findings?

options.E: Androgen-driven sebum excess with follicular plugging

whyNot.A: She uses **no new cosmetics** and lesions are not itchy
whyNot.B: Malassezia folliculitis is **itchy, monomorphic and on trunk**; not comedones
whyNot.C: That is **psoriasis** with scaly plaques, not comedones
whyNot.D: Would give **white patches**, not comedones or papules

answer: Androgens increase sebum and keratinisation, blocking follicles
why: Rising **androgens** at puberty enlarge sebaceous glands and cause **follicular hyperkeratinisation**. The plugged follicle forms a **comedo**, and *Cutibacterium acnes* growth in the sebum drives inflammation.

idea.rule: Acne = blocked follicle plus extra sebum under androgen drive.
also: Puberty and PCOS: androgen-driven acne
Anabolic steroids or androgen-secreting tumors: sudden severe acne
Isotretinoin works by shrinking sebaceous glands and reducing keratinisation
Topical retinoids unplug follicles

stem: A 17-year-old construction worker wears a hard hat for 10 hours daily in hot weather. Over 2 months he has developed small pustules and blackheads along his forehead where the headband sits. The lesions do not itch, his trunk is clear, his diet has not changed, and he is not outdoors more than before.
oneliner: 17M + hard hat 10 h/day + forehead pustules and comedones at headband line + clear trunk, no diet change → why there?
ask: Which of the following best explains the distribution of his lesions?

options.B: Follicular blockage from pressure, heat and friction
options.D: Allergic contact dermatitis to the headband material

whyNot.A: His **diet is unchanged** and the trunk is spared
whyNot.C: He has no more sun exposure than before and **lesions follow the headband**, not sun-exposed sites
whyNot.D: Contact allergy gives **itchy eczematous plaques**, not comedones; his lesions **do not itch**
whyNot.E: Would cause **widespread** acne with virilisation, not a headband pattern

answer: Occlusion and friction from the helmet plug follicles (acne mechanica)
why: **Pressure, heat, sweat and friction** at the contact site occlude follicles and promote comedone formation and inflammation. The lesions **follow the equipment**, which is the clue.

idea.rule: Mechanical occlusion over skin worsens acne at the contact site.
also: Football pads, chin straps, backpack straps
Violin held under the chin
Phones or hands pressed to the face
Occlusive cosmetics and oils (acne cosmetica)

stem: An 18-month-old boy develops severe blistering sunburn after brief sun exposure. His face and hands show dry skin with dense freckling and a mix of hypopigmented and hyperpigmented macules. His development is normal.
oneliner: 18-month-old boy + blistering after brief sun + dense freckling, dry skin with mixed pigmentation on sun-exposed skin → which repair process is impaired?
ask: Which of the following DNA repair processes is most likely defective?

whyNot.A: Fixes **small base damage** (deamination, oxidation), not UV dimers
whyNot.C: Fixes **replication errors**, defective in Lynch syndrome
whyNot.D: Repairs **double-strand breaks**, defective in some immunodeficiencies

answer: Defective nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced thymine dimers
why: **UV light** causes **pyrimidine (thymine) dimers**, which are removed by **nucleotide excision repair**. A defect leaves dimers in the DNA, causing **extreme photosensitivity, freckling and skin cancers** at a young age (**xeroderma pigmentosum**).

idea.rule: Each DNA repair pathway fixes one kind of damage; XP = defective nucleotide excision repair of UV dimers.
also: Autosomal recessive; sun avoidance
Basal and squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma
Cockayne syndrome: also NER defect
Lynch: mismatch repair; BRCA: homologous recombination

stem: A 33-year-old woman went hiking 36 hours ago and now has intensely itchy streaks of small fluid-filled bumps on her forearms and shins. She had a similar rash after hiking last summer. She has no hives, wheeze or fever, and the rash did not appear within minutes of the exposure. A photograph of her forearm is shown.
oneliner: 33F + hiking 36 h ago + itchy streaks of vesicles on forearm and shin + similar rash last summer + no hives, wheeze or fever + onset 36 h not minutes → mechanism?
ask: Which of the following best explains the rash?

options.B: Immune complex deposition in dermal vessels
options.C: Delayed response of sensitised T cells to a hapten-modified skin protein

whyNot.B: Gives **palpable purpura** (vasculitis), not itchy vesicles in streaks
whyNot.D: That is **acute bacterial infection** or pustular disease; no fever or pus
whyNot.E: Pemphigus gives **flaccid, painful blisters and mouth erosions**, not linear streaks after a plant

answer: Allergic contact dermatitis: type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity
why: **Linear vesicles 1 to 2 days after contact with a plant, with previous episodes** = poison ivy. The oil **urushiol is a hapten** that binds skin proteins, **Langerhans cells present it**, and **CD4 T cells** drive a delayed **type IV** reaction.
chain: Langerhans cells present to CD4 T cells
Itchy linear vesicles after 24 to 72 h

idea.rule: Contact dermatitis is T-cell mediated type IV hypersensitivity: delayed, not antibody mediated.
also: Nickel in jewellery or belt buckles
Neomycin and other topical drugs
Tuberculin (PPD) skin test
Contrast: type I (IgE) gives hives within minutes

image.prompt: Clinical photograph of an adult woman's forearm showing linear streaks of erythematous papules and small clear vesicles, some with crusting, on slightly swollen skin. Neutral background, forearm only. No text, labels or arrows.

stem: A 54-year-old woman with fine wrinkles and sun-damaged skin applies tretinoin daily. After 6 months, a biopsy shows more dermal collagen and a thicker epidermis than before.
oneliner: 54F + photodamaged skin with fine wrinkles + daily tretinoin 6 mo + biopsy: more dermal collagen, thicker epidermis → mechanism?
ask: Which of the following best explains the increase in collagen?

options.B: Activation of a membrane tyrosine kinase receptor
options.D: Binding to nuclear receptors that alter gene transcription in fibroblasts
options.E: Direct protection of keratinocytes from UVB

whyNot.A: Retinoids work through **nuclear receptors**, not cAMP
whyNot.B: Retinoic acid is **lipid-soluble** and acts on receptors **inside the nucleus**, not at a surface kinase
whyNot.C: Retinoids **reduce** sebum output; sebum does not build collagen
whyNot.E: Tretinoin is **not a sunscreen**; photoprotection needs UV blockers

answer: Retinoic acid acts on RAR/RXR nuclear receptors and changes gene transcription
why: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) enters cells and **binds nuclear retinoic acid receptors**. The complex **switches on genes** that raise **collagen synthesis in fibroblasts** and speed **epidermal turnover**.

idea.rule: Retinoids, steroids, thyroid hormone and vitamin D act through nuclear receptors to change transcription.
also: Glucocorticoids and sex steroids
Thyroid hormone (T3) on its nuclear receptor
Calcitriol on the vitamin D receptor
Isotretinoin and bexarotene (RXR) use the same receptor family

stem: A 41-year-old man had a coronary bypass through a median sternotomy 3 months ago. The incision has healed but the scar is now raised, firm and itchy, and has grown about 6 mm beyond the edges of the original incision. A photograph of the scar is shown.
oneliner: 41M + sternotomy 3 mo ago + raised firm itchy scar + 6 mm beyond the incision margins + photo → what drives the scar growth?
ask: Which of the following best explains the scar's growth?

whyNot.A: The **epidermis re-forms** over the wound in days; it does not build a raised dermal mass
whyNot.B: Fibrin is the **early clot scaffold**, replaced within days
whyNot.D: Granulation tissue appears in **days 3 to 14**; at 3 months it is mature scar
whyNot.E: Neutrophils dominate the **first 1 to 2 days** of healing

answer: Keloid: excessive collagen deposition extending beyond the original wound
why: After the inflammatory and granulation phases, **fibroblasts normally stop making collagen**. In a keloid they **keep depositing thick, disorganised collagen (type I)**, so the scar **extends beyond the wound** edges. Hypertrophic scars stay within the wound.

idea.rule: Keloid = excess collagen beyond the wound edges; hypertrophic scar = excess collagen within them.
also: More common in darker skin
Sites: earlobe, sternum, shoulders
Type III collagen early, replaced by type I in mature scar
Treatment: intralesional steroid, excision with radiation

image.prompt: Clinical photograph of an adult man's central upper chest showing a long, raised, firm, shiny pink-purple linear scar over the sternum that bulges outward and spreads beyond the margins of the original incision line. Skin otherwise normal. No text, labels or arrows.

stem: A 32-year-old woman develops an itchy, vesicular rash on her wrist beneath a new nickel-containing bracelet, with the full reaction appearing 48 hours after contact. Naive T cells in the draining node first meet nickel-modified peptide on MHC.
oneliner: 32F + itchy vesicular wrist rash 48 h after new nickel bracelet + naive T-cell priming → which second signal?
ask: Which receptor-ligand pair supplies the costimulatory second signal for these naive T cells?

options.A: CD40 on the APC with CD40L on the T cell
options.B: LFA-1 on the T cell with ICAM-1 on the APC
options.C: CD28 on the T cell with B7 on the APC
options.D: CTLA-4 on the T cell with B7 on the APC
options.E: PD-1 on the T cell with PD-L1 on the APC

whyNot.A: **Licenses the APC** and helps B-cell switching; it is not the T-cell second signal
whyNot.B: An **adhesion** pair that stabilises contact, not costimulation

answer: CD28 on T cell binding CD80/B7 on APC
why: This is a **type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity**. Naive T cells need **signal 1** (TCR-MHC with hapten peptide) and **signal 2**, **CD28 binding B7 (CD80/86)**, to activate; without it they become anergic.
chain: Th1 cells activate and release IFN-gamma

idea.rule: Naive T cells need two signals: TCR-MHC plus CD28-B7. Signal 1 alone gives anergy.
also: Priming in nickel or poison ivy contact dermatitis
Dendritic cells priming naive CD8 T cells
Self-antigen on cells without B7 causes anergy
CTLA-4 competes for B7 to end activation
